newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Lebed flies south for meeting on Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed flies south for meeting on Chechnya.

text.p: Security tsar Alexander Lebed flew to the ethnic republic on Ingushetia on Friday to meet leaders of southern Russian regions in an attempt to rally support for his peace drive in breakaway Chechnya.

Itar-Tass news agency said that separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev and his chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov were expected at the meeting in Nazran, the capital of Ingushetia which borders Chechnya.
The head of Chechnya's pro-Moscow administration, Doku Zavgayev, was not invited, Tass said.

Lebed, whom President Boris Yeltsin ordered to restore peace in Chechnya, struck a deal with Maskhadov on August 31 which ended 21 months of fighting in the region and followed a series of humiliating defeats for Russian troops.

The deal also postponed a decision on Chechnya's future political status by five years. The separatists say the deferral was meant to give Russia a face-saving chance to let Chechnya go rather than to give them time to change their minds.
The deal got a mixed reaction in Moscow, where many politicians said it amounted to capitulation by Russia and could encourage separatism in other parts of the country.

Lebed complains that he had little backing in his peace efforts from other officials in Moscow who, he says, have adopted a "wait-and-see" position while Yeltsin is in hospital expecting heart surgery.
